c.tagline: The Ottoman Empire's second capital, crowned by Sinan's masterpiece mosque.

taxi.fareNote: Yellow taxis are metered ('taksimetre'); confirm the meter is running, as short tourist trips are sometimes negotiated flat-rate instead.

emergency.note: 112 is the unified national emergency number in Türkiye, covering police, ambulance, and fire.

hood_landmark.Karaagac: Lausanne Monument and old Karaagac train station
hood_landmark.Sarayici: Kirkpinar wrestling arena and Edirne Palace ruins

hood_desc: Edirne's historic core, dominated by Mimar Sinan's UNESCO-listed Selimiye Mosque and the older Uc Serefeli and Eski Camii mosques. Cobbled streets are lined with Ottoman-era shops, tea houses, and the covered bazaar.

A leafy district just across the Meric River, once the terminus of the Orient Express line; the old train station now houses a university fine arts faculty. Riverside parks and the Lausanne Monument make it a peaceful escape from the center.

An island in the Tunca River that once held the sprawling Edirne Palace, now largely ruins, and today hosts the centuries-old Kirkpinar oil-wrestling festival each summer. It's a quieter, green area popular for walks along the water.

A residential neighborhood spreading north of the center, mixing everyday apartment blocks with local markets and neighborhood mosques. It offers a glimpse of ordinary Edirne life away from the monuments.
A mixed commercial-residential district with small shops, bakeries, and produce markets serving locals rather than tourists. It sits within easy walking or a short dolmus ride of the historic center.

water.note: Locals and visitors alike drink bottled water rather than tap.

transit.map: Edirne Belediyesi municipal bus route maps
transit.note: Edirne's historic core is small and very walkable; dolmus minibuses cover outer neighborhoods and nearby villages.

train: Limited passenger rail; most travelers use intercity buses

tip.r: A small tip of 5-10% in restaurants is appreciated; rounding up taxi fares is common.
